Commit - The earlier DDBDP version of the text had ἐντ(ὸς) at the beginning of most lines, but this cannot be upheld. It was not even Bell’s intention; cf. the lemma in 15 n., χω(ριω) Παπλοου, and 54 n., where ἐν τ(ῇ) κώμῃ is cited from lin60. I have replaced ἐντ(ὸς) with ἐν τ(ῷ) / τ(ῇ) throughout. In lin13 it seems safe to read ἐν τ(ῷ) Ἁγί\ου/ Ἰωάννο\υ/, scil. μοναστηρίῳ (I have discussed this with F. Morelli). The same perhaps holds for lin75, ἐν τ(ῷ) Τερύθ[ε(ως), scil. χωρίῳ, but I’ve opted for the cautious ἐν τ( ) Τερύθ[ε( ). In lins54 and 59, the implication of reading Τ̣ο̣[ε]τ̣ω and [Τ]ο̣ετω (readings confirmed on an image), a village, is that [εἰ(ς) τ(ὴν) παγαρχ(ίαν)] is impossible; removed and lacuna left unrestored. An oddity is lin14 (εἰ(ς)) (τ(ὸ)) <:νοτινὸν σκέλος|reg|νοτιν\οῦ/ (σκέλου(ς)):>.

Vote - Accept-Straight-to-Finalization - lin1 et passim: not ἐντ(ὸς) but ἐν τ(ῷ) + dative; cf 43 ἐν τ(ῇ) πόλει. || lin53 <:(υἱ(οὶ))|reg|υἱυὶ:>: write (υἱ(οὶ)); υιυι indicates the plural, and it's not a misspelling.
